title: How to Care for Your Soy Candles
excerpt: Make your handmade soy candles last longer and burn better with these simple care tips from our artisan.
content:
Your soy candle is a handmade treasure, poured in a small batch and finished by hand. A little care on every burn keeps it burning clean, smelling beautiful and lasting right to the bottom of the jar.

Make the first burn count. The first time you light your candle, let it burn until the melted wax reaches the edges of the jar, usually two to three hours. Soy wax has a memory: if you blow it out early, it will keep melting only that narrow circle and tunnel down the middle.

Trim the wick to about 1/4 inch before every burn. A short wick gives a calm, steady flame. A long one flickers, smokes and leaves black soot on the glass.

Keep each burn under four hours, and keep the candle away from fans, open windows and air conditioners. Draughts make the flame dance, which uses up wax unevenly and dulls the scent.

Stop when about half an inch of wax is left at the bottom, so the glass doesn’t overheat. Once it has cooled, scoop out the last of the wax with a spoon, wash the jar in warm soapy water, and give it a second life as a planter, a pen holder or a home for your jewellery.

And always: never leave a burning candle unattended, and keep it out of reach of children and pets.
author: Sparsh Divine Art Studio

title: The Story Behind Our Resin Art
excerpt: How a passion for preserving nature's beauty led to our stunning resin art collection.
content:
Every piece of resin art we create starts with a flower picked at its most beautiful: a rose from a wedding bouquet, a marigold from a festival, a sprig of baby’s breath from a garden.

The flowers are pressed or air-dried for one to three weeks, depending on how delicate they are. This is the slowest part of the process and the one we never rush, because any moisture left inside a petal turns brown once it is sealed.

Then we pour. Resin goes in thin layers, each one left to cure before the next, so the flowers can be placed exactly where they look best and the finished piece stays crystal clear without bubbles. A serving tray can take four or five layers and almost a week to fully cure.

Finally every piece is sanded, polished and checked by hand. Because real botanicals are never exactly alike, no two trays, bookmarks or keychains are ever the same.

Many of our favourite pieces are custom orders: flowers from a wedding, a first anniversary or a loved one’s garden, preserved so they can be kept for years. If you have flowers you want to keep, message us before they dry out completely, and we will tell you how to store them until they reach us.

title: Ultimate Diwali Gift Guide 2024
excerpt: Finding the perfect Diwali gift has never been easier. Here's our curated guide for every budget.
content:
Diwali is the festival of lights, love and togetherness. This year, give a gift that is made by hand and chosen with care, something that will still be on display long after the sweets are gone.

For family, a gift hamper brings several of our handmade pieces together in one beautifully packed box, ready to give.

For hosts, a pair of candles in warm, festive scents makes an elegant thank-you when you visit for puja or dinner. Pair it with a handwritten note and it needs no other wrapping.

For colleagues and clients, small candles and resin keychains can be customised with names or a logo. We take bulk orders, so get in touch early in October so there is time to craft and deliver them all.

For yourself: light a candle while you clean, decorate and draw the rangoli. You have earned it.

Custom and bulk orders get busy in the weeks before Diwali. Order early to make sure everything arrives well before the festival.
